clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:
Section 1. E s t a b lis h m e n t , (a) There is established a Presidential Commission  
on Indian Reservation Economies.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) The Commission shall be com posed of no more than nine members, who  
shall be appointed by the President from among the private sector, reservation  
tribal governments, econom ic academ icians, and Federal employees.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) The President shall designate a non-Indian representative and an Indian  
representative to serve as cochairm en of the Commission.

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. F u n c t io n s , (a) The Commission shall advise the President on w hat  
actions should be taken to develop a stronger private sector on Federally  
recognized Indian reservations, lessen tribal dependence on Federal monies  
and programs and reduce the Federal presence in Indian affairs. The underly­
ing principles of this mission are the govem m ent-to-govem m ent relationship,  
the established Federal policy of self-determination and the Federal trust  
responsibility.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) The Commission will focus exclusively on the following items, and not on  
new Federal financial assistance:

(1) Defining the existing Federal legislative, regulatory, and procedural obsta­
cles to the creation of positive econom ic environments on Indian reservations.

(2) Identifying and recommending changes or other remedial actions necessary  
to remove these obstacles.

(3) Defining the obstacles at the State, local and tribal government levels  
which impede both Indian and non-Indian private sector investments on  
reservations.

(4) Identifying actions which these levels of government could take to rectify  
the identified problems.

(5) Recommending w ays for the private sector, both Indian and non-Indian, to  
participate in the development and growth of reservation economies, including  
capital formation.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) The Commission should review  studies undertaken in the last decade to  
obtain pertinent recom m endations that are directly related to its mission.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text:
(d) The Commission shall, unless sooner extended, submit a final report to the  
President and to the Secretary of the Interior within six months after appoint­
ment of the last Commissioner, or by September 30, 1983, w hichever com es  
earlier.

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. A d m in is t r a t io n , (a) The heads of-Executive agencies shall, to the extent  
permitted by law, provide the Commission with such information as m ay be  
necessary for the effective perform ance of its functions.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) Members of the Commission m ay receive com pensation for their work on  
the Commission. W hile engaged in the work of the Commission members m ay

=== PDF page 202 of 208 ===
2310 Federal Register /  Vol. 48, No. 12 /  Tuesday, January 18, 1983 /  Presidential Documents
be allowed travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of subsistence, as  
authorized by law  for persons serving intermittently in the government service  
(5 U.S.C. 5701-5707).

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) The Secretary of the Interior shall, to the extent permitted by law  and  
subject to the availability of funds, provide the Commission with such admin­
istrative services, funds, facilities, staff and other support services as m ay be  
necessary for the effective performance of its functions.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text:
(d) The Commission will m eet approximately 15 times at the call of the  
chairmen. All meetings of the Commission and all agenda must have prior  
approval of the chairmen.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text: (e) In carrying out its responsibilities, the Commission is authorized to:

(1) Conduct hearings, interviews, and reviews at field sites, or wherever  
deemed necessary to fulfill its duties.

(2) Confer with Indian tribal government officials and members, private sector  
business officials and managers, and other parties dealing with matters  
pertaining to the Commission’s mission.

clauses.label: Sec. 4.
clauses.text:
Sec. 4. G e n e r a l P r o v is io n s , (a) Notwithstanding the provisions of any other  
Executive order, the responsibilities of the President under the Federal Advi­
sory Committee A ct, as amended, except that of reporting annually to the  
Congress, which are applicable to the advisory commission established by  
this Order, shall be performed by the Secretary of the Interior, in accordance  
with the guidelines and procedures established by the Administrator of  
General Services.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) The Commission shall terminate 60 days after it transmits its final report to  
the President, or on D ecember 31,1983, w hichever com es earlier.

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec1.label: Section 1.
CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec1.text:
Section 1. E s t a b lis h m e n t , (a) There is established a Presidential Commission  
on Indian Reservation Economies.

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec1-b.label: (b)
CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec1-b.text:
(b) The Commission shall be com posed of no more than nine members, who  
shall be appointed by the President from among the private sector, reservation  
tribal governments, econom ic academ icians, and Federal employees.

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec1-c.label: (c)
CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec1-c.text:
(c) The President shall designate a non-Indian representative and an Indian  
representative to serve as cochairm en of the Commission.

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec2.label: Sec. 2.
CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec2.text:
Sec. 2. F u n c t io n s , (a) The Commission shall advise the President on w hat  
actions should be taken to develop a stronger private sector on Federally  
recognized Indian reservations, lessen tribal dependence on Federal monies  
and programs and reduce the Federal presence in Indian affairs. The underly­
ing principles of this mission are the govem m ent-to-govem m ent relationship,  
the established Federal policy of self-determination and the Federal trust  
responsibility.

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec2-b.label: (b)
CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec2-b.text:
(b) The Commission will focus exclusively on the following items, and not on  
new Federal financial assistance:

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec2-b-1.text:
(1) Defining the existing Federal legislative, regulatory, and procedural obsta­
cles to the creation of positive econom ic environments on Indian reservations.

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec2-b-2.text:
(2) Identifying and recommending changes or other remedial actions necessary  
to remove these obstacles.

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec2-b-3.text:
(3) Defining the obstacles at the State, local and tribal government levels  
which impede both Indian and non-Indian private sector investments on  
reservations.

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec2-b-4.text:
(4) Identifying actions which these levels of government could take to rectify  
the identified problems.

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec2-b-5.text:
(5) Recommending w ays for the private sector, both Indian and non-Indian, to  
participate in the development and growth of reservation economies, including  
capital formation.

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec2-c.label: (c)
CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec2-c.text:
(c) The Commission should review  studies undertaken in the last decade to  
obtain pertinent recom m endations that are directly related to its mission.

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec2-d.label: (d)
CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec2-d.text:
(d) The Commission shall, unless sooner extended, submit a final report to the  
President and to the Secretary of the Interior within six months after appoint­
ment of the last Commissioner, or by September 30, 1983, w hichever com es  
earlier.

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec3.label: Sec. 3.
CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec3.text:
Sec. 3. A d m in is t r a t io n , (a) The heads of-Executive agencies shall, to the extent  
permitted by law, provide the Commission with such information as m ay be  
necessary for the effective perform ance of its functions.

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec3-b.label: (b)
CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec3-b.text:
(b) Members of the Commission m ay receive com pensation for their work on  
the Commission. W hile engaged in the work of the Commission members m ay

be allowed travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of subsistence, as  
authorized by law  for persons serving intermittently in the government service  
(5 U.S.C. 5701-5707).

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec3-c.label: (c)
CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec3-c.text:
(c) The Secretary of the Interior shall, to the extent permitted by law  and  
subject to the availability of funds, provide the Commission with such admin­
istrative services, funds, facilities, staff and other support services as m ay be  
necessary for the effective performance of its functions.

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec3-d.label: (d)
CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec3-d.text:
(d) The Commission will m eet approximately 15 times at the call of the  
chairmen. All meetings of the Commission and all agenda must have prior  
approval of the chairmen.

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec3-e.label: (e)
CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec3-e.text: (e) In carrying out its responsibilities, the Commission is authorized to:

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec3-e-1.text:
(1) Conduct hearings, interviews, and reviews at field sites, or wherever  
deemed necessary to fulfill its duties.

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec3-e-2.text:
(2) Confer with Indian tribal government officials and members, private sector  
business officials and managers, and other parties dealing with matters  
pertaining to the Commission’s mission.

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec4.label: Sec. 4.
CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec4.text:
Sec. 4. G e n e r a l P r o v is io n s , (a) Notwithstanding the provisions of any other  
Executive order, the responsibilities of the President under the Federal Advi­
sory Committee A ct, as amended, except that of reporting annually to the  
Congress, which are applicable to the advisory commission established by  
this Order, shall be performed by the Secretary of the Interior, in accordance  
with the guidelines and procedures established by the Administrator of  
General Services.

CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec4-b.label: (b)
CLAUSES:EO:12401#sec4-b.text:
(b) The Commission shall terminate 60 days after it transmits its final report to  
the President, or on D ecember 31,1983, w hichever com es earlier.
